newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate up, shadows U.S. long bond yield.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate up, shadows U.S. long bond yield.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates gained 30 basis points to trade at 23.70 percent in early trade on Wednesday in parallel with U.S. long bond yields, traders said.
"U.S. industrial output figures were strong and the U.S. long bond reacted, which is exerting pressure on the (domestic) secondary market," a trader said.
The U.S. 30-year Treasury bond was, meanwhile, off 14/32 to 7.13 percent.
Some traders said the market was slow on caution over early weakness on the peso. Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts were unchanged at 7.8960/7.9000 per dollar, but had opened 0.45 of a centavo weaker.

Dealers expected secondary rates to remain stable during the session as Wednesday saw the monthly cut-off data for banks to settle outstanding balances on checking accounts they hold with the central bank.
"Every one needs to square positions today to meet the cutoff date, so they will have to cover shorts or sell longs," a trader said.
Overnight rates on bank paper were 19 basis points at 25.71 percent.
Liquidity of 6.917 billion pesos was programmed to return to the system from prior central bank participation.
